doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: More chord demonstration, Huntington and Schaff, and the first recording with George
summary: Marrero finishes the chord demonstration, talks again about Huntington and Schaff, and mentions wanting a band and the first recording made with George.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, the second finger, two and barring all three of them. Barring three? Yeah. And then, you see, of course I know we can't do it all night, but I would like to show you how to make right from there to jump in your seventh chord. Man, them boys play something. Man, sure. Who was that Bill Huntington? Huntington and then John Schaff. That's true. No. Man, the boys play something bad. But Bill is more of a jazz band you play than Bill, or Schaff is, but Schaff is, no more music, is it? He said, I'm going to run, man. You know, he had nothing but string instruments. Now he teaches himself now. He teaches banjo. Right? Yeah, he had about four fellas around him, four bands that played around him, man. He'd make records too. Boy, you ought to hear them boys. He want to come down here sometime, but man, he keep me up too long. I said, no, John, I can't make it. John, I said, you're until 12 o'clock at night, man. Come on down, you make all the different keys the same way. Now, instead of making the seventh now, you're going to make natural. Now, see, that's Db. Now, come up higher. Or C-sharp. That's Db, C-sharp, yeah. Now, come up higher. Now, that will be D natural. D natural. Next one will be Db. E flat. Next one will be D natural. And then F. F. F. I'm glad you like it. You like it. You know, once you like something, boy, you pay more attention to it. Had my mind to put me up a good band, because then, in God, you need to go traveling all the time. Traveling, I don't want to go too far away from home no more. You know, I'm afraid that I get sick of something a little over me bad. Yeah, that's where George come got me from. The first recording we made was Gene, William. We made up there on Broom Wall, remember?
